thread:
Alex Chen: Heads up — seeing a heat spike in az3 GPU rack cluster-7 over the last 20m. I want to schedule a rolling drain + reboot window tonight 00:30->02:30 UTC for affected hosts.
Rachel Kim: timeline okay for APAC customers? nighttime there but call it out in comms.
Alex Chen: yes APAC low traffic. plan: cohort drains of 10 nodes at a time, 5m stagger, KV cache seed on warm hosts, autoscaler set to hold burst pool. expected ~2x token cost for 30m per cohort while backfills run.
Samir Patel: cost question — if we shift some jobs to the non-preemptible dedicated pool we blow reserved capacity. can we instead route lower-priority jobs to spot gradient pool?
Jia Liu: we can. propose rule: route any tenant tagged `noncritical` to spot-burst during window, keep `priority:enterprise` on primary with failover to smaller quantized model to preserve SLA.
Alex Chen: good. i'll add a routing override in the policy: `route_on_thermal_spike: true` with fallback to `gptq-8b` variants for priority paths.
Rachel Kim: add customer comm: explain brief degradation risk and expected window, mention fallback models. also include contact for SLA ops.
Samir Patel: also note throughput reduction for embeddings pipelines. estimate increase in per-embedding latency from 40ms -> 120ms during cohorts. budget impact ~+$1.2k for 2h across cluster.
Alex Chen: noted. ops runbook steps (short):
````
1. mark cohort nodes `drain` via fleet-cli: `fleet drain --cohort c7 --limit 10`
2. monitor `gpu_temp`, `packet_loss`, `kv_hit_rate` dashboards
3. seed kv-cache: `kvseed --targets warm`
4. toggle routing for noncritical tenants
5. roll to next cohort after 15m steady metrics
````
Jia Liu: small ask — can we bump up `prefill_concurrency` to 2 during seed to reduce cold-start latencies? Test on one cohort first.
Alex Chen: yes — prod ramp will be: prefill_concurrency=1 -> observe -> 2. test on cohort-1 00:35 UTC.
infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance window created: id=mnt-az3-1799990001 window=2026-03-23T00:30:00Z-2026-03-23T02:30:00Z creator=Alex Chen.
Rachel Kim: i'll draft the slack+email comms and post to #customer-success + status page 00:00 UTC. include mitigation steps and expected cost delta.
Samir Patel: If thermal doesn't improve after two cohorts, plan B is to escalate to rack-level PDU swap. that will be daytime and higher customer impact — we should avoid.
Jia Liu: I'll prepare rollback commands and a smoke test prompt set for quality checks post-evac.
Alex Chen: thanks — i'll run canary on cohort-1, post results in 15m before rolling. ping @here when drains start. :thumbsup:
